cover.headline_html: 3 myths that stop small businesses cold.

myths.label: The Scale Illusion
myths.myth_text: Federal contracts are for big corporations — small businesses can't compete at that level.
myths.reality_text: Small businesses took $16.6B in Q2 2026 alone — IT, engineering, construction, professional services. The money is real. The barrier is paperwork, not odds. Source · USAspending.gov

myths.label: The Past-Performance Trap
myths.myth_text: You need a federal track record before any agency will look at you.
myths.reality_text: Teaming agreements let new shops compete under an established prime's history. Subcontracting builds your own record while you're still learning how the market moves.

myths.label: The Schedule Sells Itself
myths.myth_text: Getting on the GSA Schedule means the contracts start coming automatically.
myths.reality_text: The Schedule is a buying vehicle, not a sales engine. It opens the door — you still have to market, build relationships, and respond to RFQs. Most new holders go quiet and wonder why nothing lands.

close.close_question: Drop the myth you believed when you first looked at federal contracting.
